VENDOR AGREEMENT

THIS VENDOR AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into effective as of January 1, 2023 (the "Effective Date"), by and between GREENLINE DISPOSAL SERVICES, LLC, a Texas limited liability company ("Contractor"), and MERIDIAN MECHANICAL OF TEXAS, LLC, a Texas limited liability company located at 10850 West Little York Road, Houston, Texas 77041 ("Customer").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Contractor provides waste, scrap metal, and recycling services in the State of Texas; and

WHEREAS, Customer operates mechanical contracting businesses at multiple locations throughout Texas and requires comprehensive waste management and scrap metal recovery services; and

WHEREAS, Contractor and Customer desire to enter into this Agreement whereby Contractor shall provide waste, scrap metal, and recycling services to Customer's facilities in Houston, San Antonio, and Dallas, Texas, upon the terms and conditions set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, Contractor and Customer agree as follows:

1. SERVICES

1.1 Scope of Services. Contractor shall provide comprehensive waste, scrap metal, and recycling collection, handling, transportation, and disposal services for Customer's operations at the following locations: Meridian Mechanical Houston facility located at 10850 West Little York Road, Houston, Texas 77041; Meridian Mechanical San Antonio facility located at 1423 South General McMullen Drive, San Antonio, Texas 78202; and Meridian Mechanical Dallas facility located at 4747 North Stemmons Freeway, Dallas, Texas 75247 (collectively, the "Facilities"). Services shall include, without limitation, the collection of general waste, scrap copper, ferrous metals, aluminum, and miscellaneous recyclable materials generated in the ordinary course of Customer's mechanical contracting operations.

1.2 Service Schedule. Contractor shall provide pickup services at each Facility on a weekly basis, or more frequently if requested by Customer. Contractor shall maintain adequate dumpsters or collection containers at each Facility to accommodate typical waste streams. Customer shall provide written notice to Contractor if additional pickup services are needed, and Contractor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate such requests within three business days.

1.3 Contractor Responsibilities. Contractor shall be responsible for providing all containers and collection equipment, arranging for timely pickup and transportation of waste and recyclable materials, ensuring proper handling and sorting of scrap materials, and complying with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations. Contractor shall maintain all necessary licenses, permits, and insurance coverage required to perform the services described herein.

1.4 Customer Responsibilities. Customer shall segregate scrap materials to the extent commercially practicable, placing ferrous metals, non-ferrous metals, and general waste in appropriate designated containers provided by Contractor. Customer shall not place hazardous materials, including but not limited to oils, coolants, solvents, and electrical components, in collection containers without prior written approval from Contractor and compliance with applicable disposal regulations.

2. SCRAP METAL REBATE

2.1 Copper Rebate Program. For all scrap copper materials collected from the Facilities, Contractor shall provide Customer with a monthly rebate calculated as follows: eighty-two percent (82%) of the COMEX HG (high-grade copper) spot price per pound, less a processing and handling deduction of thirty-five cents ($0.35) per pound.

2.2 Pricing Mechanism. The COMEX HG spot price shall be determined using the settlement price published by the COMEX division of the New York Mercantile Exchange on the last business day of each calendar month. In the event that the COMEX exchange is closed on the final business day of any month, the settlement price from the preceding business day shall be used. Contractor shall provide Customer with written documentation of the applicable pricing, weight, and rebate calculation no later than the fifteenth (15th) day following the end of each calendar month.

2.3 Weight Certification. All scrap copper shall be weighed at Contractor's certified scales located at Contractor's primary facility in Houston, Texas. Customer shall have the right, upon reasonable notice, to witness the weighing of materials and to obtain copies of weight tickets for Customer's records. Contractor shall maintain detailed records of all materials received from Customer for a period of no less than three (3) years.

2.4 Other Scrap Materials. For ferrous metals, aluminum, and other non-copper scrap materials collected from the Facilities, Contractor shall retain all recovery value. No rebate or payment shall be due to Customer for such materials.

3. CHARGES AND SURCHARGES

3.1 Service Charges. Customer shall pay Contractor a base service charge of Nine Hundred Fifty Dollars ($950.00) per month per Facility for waste collection and disposal services. This base charge covers weekly pickups and standard disposal of general waste materials generated at normal volumes consistent with Customer's historical waste production.

3.2 Fuel Surcharge. In addition to the base service charge, Customer shall pay a fuel surcharge of seven dollars and fifty cents ($7.50) per pickup per Facility, which surcharge shall be adjusted quarterly on the first day of January, April, July, and October based on the average price of unleaded regular gasoline in the Houston metropolitan area as published by the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The fuel surcharge shall be adjusted within a range of five dollars and twenty-five cents ($5.25) to ten dollars and seventy-five cents ($10.75) per pickup based on prevailing fuel costs.

3.3 Environmental Recovery Surcharge. Contractor shall charge an environmental recovery surcharge of twelve dollars ($12.00) per ton of waste and recyclable materials collected, which surcharge is designated to cover the costs of environmental compliance, regulatory permits, hazardous waste handling protocols, and ongoing environmental remediation programs. This surcharge shall be reviewed annually and may be adjusted upon sixty (60) days' written notice to Customer if material changes in environmental regulatory requirements or disposal costs occur.

3.4 Excess Volume Charges. Should Customer place more than the standard amount of waste in collection containers between scheduled pickups, resulting in overflow or requiring additional pickups beyond the weekly schedule, Customer shall be charged an additional pickup fee of Two Hundred Dollars ($200.00) per additional pickup per Facility.

3.5 Hazardous Waste Handling. If Customer places hazardous materials or substances requiring special handling in collection containers without prior authorization, Contractor may charge Customer a hazardous waste remediation fee of Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00) per incident, plus the actual cost of specialized disposal or remediation services required.

4. PAYMENT TERMS

4.1 Invoicing and Payment. Contractor shall invoice Customer monthly for base service charges, surcharges, and applicable rebates. Invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of invoice date. Contractor shall deduct any copper rebate amounts owed to Customer from the total invoice amount, or, at Customer's election, shall pay rebates by separate check within the same thirty-day payment period.

4.2 Late Payment. If any invoice remains unpaid more than thirty (30) days after the invoice date, Contractor may charge interest on the outstanding balance at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by Texas law, whichever is less. Additionally, Contractor may suspend services upon ten (10) days' written notice if payment is more than thirty (30) days past due.

4.3 Pricing Adjustments. Base service charges and environmental recovery surcharges may be adjusted annually on January 1 of each contract year upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to Customer. Such adjustments shall not exceed five percent (5%) per annum without mutual written consent of both parties.

5. TERM

5.1 Initial Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of three (3) years, expiring on December 31, 2025 (the "Initial Term"), unless sooner terminated in accordance with the provisions hereof.

5.2 Renewal. This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term.

5.3 Early Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement prior to the expiration of the Initial Term only for material breach by the other party, provided that the breaching party is given thirty (30) days' written notice specifying the nature of the breach and a reasonable opportunity to cure. If the breach is not cured within such thirty-day period, the non-breaching party may terminate this Agreement upon an additional ten (10) days' written notice.

6. TERM CONTINUATION AND CHANGES

6.1 Effect of Expiration. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, Contractor shall remove all collection containers and equipment from the Facilities within five (5) business days. Customer shall have removed all recyclable and waste materials from containers prior to removal. Customer shall pay all outstanding invoices and charges within thirty (30) days of termination.

7. CONFIDENTIALITY

7.1 Confidential Information. Each party acknowledges that it may receive confidential business information from the other party, including pricing, customer lists, and operational procedures. Each party agrees to maintain the confidentiality of such information and not to disclose it to third parties without prior written consent, except as required by law or court order.

8. INSURANCE AND LIABILITY

8.1 Contractor Insurance. Contractor shall maintain, at its sole expense, comprehensive general liability insurance with minimum coverage of One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) in aggregate, covering bodily injury and property damage. Contractor shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance upon request.

8.2 Limitation of Liability. Neither party shall be liable to the other for indirect, incidental, consequential, or punitive damages, regardless of the cause of action, even if advised of the possibility of such damages. Each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the total amounts paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim.

9. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

9.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to its conflicts of laws principles. All disputes arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Harris County, Texas.

9.2 Dispute Resolution. Prior to initiating litigation, the parties agree to attempt to resolve any dispute through good faith negotiation by representatives with authority to settle. If negotiation fails within thirty (30) days, either party may pursue legal remedies available under Texas law.

10. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

10.1 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with any amendments or exhibits attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties concerning the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior understandings and agreements, whether oral or written.

10.2 Amendment. This Agreement may be amended only by written instrument executed by authorized representatives of both parties.

10.3 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

10.4 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

10.5 Notices. All notices required under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered personally, by email with confirmation of receipt, or by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the addresses set forth herein or such other addresses as either party may designate by written notice.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.
